## Trigger Event On 2026-08-17 story B-7dff finished all five checklist items, resolved ten review findings across four rounds and collected four reviewer passes on its final tree, then failed to enter DONE. Its done_required_validate emitted status FAIL with reasons command-failed: FAIL root full test suite: npm test exitCode=1, while the same run logged full-suite: 47/47 passed in 335.4s and full-suite performance budget exceeded: 335410.6ms >= 300000ms. No member failed. The gate rejected a green suite because the machine is slower than the constant assumed. ## Key Insights The problem is a class, not an incident. Four separate absolute wall-clock thresholds in the same stack were each sized against a faster host: a 270000ms per-validate-command cap, a 120000ms per-suite-member default, a 300000ms whole-suite budget, and a 900000ms CLI maximum. Three of them produced false failures during a single day of work, and each was diagnosed only after someone measured rather than assumed. A clean detached worktree of main at 860b7b45cf, run on the same host in the same session, gives TIMEOUT test:flow-stability-smoke 120.0s and full-suite: 48/49 passed in 296.8s with exit 1. That comparison is what separates a pre-existing repository condition from a regression introduced by in-flight work, and it also shows the 296.8s figure is not really under budget: it fits only because a member was killed 41s early. With that member running to completion the suite is structurally about 335s here. The measurement inputs for a better guard already exist. The runner writes cpuInventory.userSeconds and systemSeconds, workerUtilization, criticalPath and a baselineComparison against historicalSerialMs 1688918. A guard expressed in accumulated CPU time, or as a ratio against a recorded baseline, would have caught the regression the 300000ms constant was meant to catch while staying silent on a merely slower machine. ## Solution Tradeoffs Option A, raise each constant: trivial and immediately unblocking, but it re-arms the same failure on the next slower host and quietly weakens a regression guard. It is what the guard author was trying to prevent. Option B, make the whole-suite guard host-relative (CPU time or baseline ratio) and give the genuinely at-risk members explicit budgets sized to measured contended duration: keeps the guard meaningful, costs real design work, and needs a defensible answer for what the new threshold means. Option C, demote the whole-suite breach to a warning and keep member failures fatal: cheapest honest option, preserves the signal for a human without failing a green suite, but loses automatic enforcement of the performance goal. The pinned-command cap is separable and much simpler: resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs should consult doneRequiredCommands as well as validate.commands, since npm test already declares 7200000ms there. ## Conversational Texture This surfaced while driving B-7dff to DONE under an instruction to follow the whole process without escalating routine calls. Three ways out of the block were available and two of them were refusals on principle rather than on cost: relabelling a deferred waiver to permanent would have cleared the ProofStory completeness gate in one field edit but was the same move a reviewer had already caught and filed as a finding earlier in that story, and editing the 300000ms budget from inside B-7dff would have meant weakening a guard to pass the story that tripped it, on a boundary that story had itself declared out of scope. The operator chose to fix the budget in its own story instead. Worth preserving: the first instinct on seeing 335s was that B-7dff had introduced a 34 percent regression, and a main-baseline run on the same host falsified that within ten minutes.

That comparison is what separates a pre-existing repository condition from a regression introduced by in-flight work, and it also shows the 296.8s figure is not really under budget: it fits only because a member was killed 41s early. With that member running to completion the suite is structurally about 335s here.

A full 107-command lattice validate hit the framework 900000ms CLI max-timeout at command 74/107, while the same plan measured 1474.9s at jobs=4 and 2225.0s at jobs=1. Operators are currently working around this by exporting LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS by hand on every closeout command, which is undocumented tribal knowledge and silently breaks anyone who forgets. Either raise or derive the default so a configured plan can complete, or make the failure state say plainly that the plan needs a larger budget and name the variable.
Decide and record whether the 900s CLI max timeout still covers a full validate run

DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS is 120000ms. test:flow-stability-smoke rides that default while measuring 150.0s standalone and 161.1s across four workers, so it times out on main today (verified on a clean detached worktree at 860b7b45cf: TIMEOUT 120.0s, 48/49 passed). test:milestone-status is the only other default rider under a 2x margin at 68.3s. Note story B-7dff already raised these two on its branch (flow-stability to 540000, milestone-status to 240000) as a targeted unblock; check what has landed before duplicating, and reconcile rather than reverting. Do not raise members that are not at risk, since an inflated budget hides a genuinely hung member.

Four absolute wall-clock thresholds in the validation stack are calibrated for a faster machine than the one the repository currently runs on, and three of them now produce false failures. Measured 2026-08-17/18 on one host in one session: 1. Whole-suite budget. isUnderFullSuiteBudget (packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts, ~line 298) hardcodes 300000ms, and fullSuiteBudgetBreached sets process.exitCode = 1 whenever jobs > 1. The suite measures 333.7s / 334.5s / 335.4s / 336.2s / 357.5s across five complete runs with every member passing, so a fully green 47/47 run exits 1. A DONE-required receipt from 2026-08-17T00:46 recorded the same suite at 221s, so the host is materially slower now than that morning. 2. Per-member default. DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS in the same file is 120000ms and test:flow-stability-smoke rides it while taking 150.0s standalone and 161.1s sharing four workers, so it cannot pass. Verified on a clean detached worktree of main at 860b7b45cf on the same host in the same session: TIMEOUT test:flow-stability-smoke 120.0s, full-suite: 48/49 passed in 296.8s, exit 1. npm test is therefore red on main independently of any story. 3. Pinned-command receipt cap. resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs (packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:46) matches only against configuredValidationCommands, so a command declared in doneRequiredCommands is invisible to it. npm test is declared there with timeoutMs 7200000 but falls back to the 270000ms default, and verification_evidence_add returns receipt_exit_nonzero exit 124 (timed out) for any intent pinned to it. The function own docstring says its purpose is to stop silently falling back to the hardcoded 270s default for commands with a deliberately higher configured budget, so this is a gap in that fix rather than new design. 4. CLI max timeout. A full 107-command lattice validate hit the framework 900s CLI max-timeout at command 74/107 while the plan itself measured 1474.9s, so the default is now below the work it has to cover. Consequence: story B-7dff is complete, has all five checklist items done, ten review findings resolved and four reviewer passes on the final tree, yet cannot enter DONE. Its done_required_validate run reports status FAIL with reasons command-failed: FAIL root full test suite: npm test exitCode=1, while the same run logs full-suite: 47/47 passed in 335.4s and budget exceeded: 335410.6ms >= 300000ms. Every member passes; only the clock fails. Explicitly NOT wanted: raising 300000 to a larger constant. A number chosen to make today host pass stops working on tomorrow host, and the guard exists to catch a real regression. The runner already records cpuInventory.userSeconds and systemSeconds and a baselineComparison against historicalSerialMs 1688918, so a host-relative or CPU-time formulation is available without inventing new measurement.

Five complete runs with every member passing measured 333.7-357.5s on the current host, against 221s recorded on 2026-08-17T00:46, so the constant now fails green suites. Do not simply raise it: the runner already records cpuInventory user/system seconds, workerUtilization and a baselineComparison against historicalSerialMs 1688918, so a CPU-time or baseline-ratio formulation is available. Whatever is chosen must still fail a genuine regression and must state what the new threshold means.
Let resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs see commands declared in doneRequiredCommands

entries.reason: Premise falsified within minutes of creation. B-2614 claimed four absolute wall-clock thresholds were miscalibrated; main at HEAD has already fixed two of them and reshaped a third. Verified directly: FULL_SUITE_BUDGET_MS = 1_200_000 (full-suite-runner.ts:316) with a documented satisfiability invariant against longestEntryTimeoutMs, withConcurrencyHeadroom(entry, jobs) at :346 applied at the call site :617, and defaultJobs(cpuCount = availableParallelism()) at :383 replacing the hardcoded 4; the CLI max timeout is now a derived effectiveMaxBudget with a reported source rather than a fixed 900s. Only two narrow items survive and they do not justify this storys framing: resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs (handlers/checklist.ts) still matches only configuredValidationCommands so a command declared in doneRequiredCommands stays on the 270000ms default, and the JSON receipt still writes performanceBudgetMs: 300_000 (full-suite-runner.ts:634) while the gate reads FULL_SUITE_BUDGET_MS, so the artifact misreports the budget it was judged against. Those will be filed as their own small story rather than carried inside a story whose stated problem no longer exists.
